A full contract never materialized, though, and now Brown has finally found a landing spot to begin his season. According to an official announcement , Brown has signed with HC Ajoie, who are based in Porrentruy, Switzerland and compete in Switzerland’s National League. Brown signed a contract that will last until the end of the 2026 calendar year. The deal contains an option to extend for the rest of the 2026-27 season. Brown is set to join a roster with several former NHL players, including former AHL MVP Daniel Carr and former Dallas Stars top prospect Julius Honka . Brown, 28, is set to begin his European pro career as a result of this signing. His professional career thus far has been spent entirely in the NHL and AHL. Last season, Brown played 31 games for the AHL’s Ontario Reign, scoring 16 points. The 2016 No. 11 overall pick has 99 NHL games and 26 points on his resume.

items.title: Canucks GM Ryan Johnson preaching patience as losses pile up
items.summary: With the rebuilding Canucks on an eight-game losing streak, GM Ryan Johnson isn’t panicking. “Before it gets better, it was going to get really hard, and we have to understand that.”
items.body: VANCOUVER — The evening before training camp opened, general manager Ryan Johnson gathered the Vancouver Canucks ’ staff and players for a dinner meeting at the team’s lakeside hotel in Penticton, and then spoke the truth. “The No. 1 thing I talked about is: ‘You have no idea how hard this is going to be,’” Johnson recalled Wednesday. “Like, ‘what you've signed up for here is almost impossible.’ You’d be ignorant... if you thought you were just going to walk in and things would fall into place. I said: ‘You’ve got to be ready because you're going to get punched in the face real quick.’ Here they are, bruised and spiralling through an eight-game losing streak and just 2-8-1 through the start of the rebuild’s first full season. In their last five games, Vancouver has been tied or led four times through 40 minutes and trailed (by a goal) once, then been outscored 11-0 in the third period while losing all of them. The rebuild is not the impossible part that Johnson referred to just five weeks ago, although there is overwhelming evidence around the National Hockey League — see the Detroit Red Wings, the Canucks’ opponents Thursday — that it will be difficult. The impossible part is believing the Canucks, under new management, with new coaches and new systems, many young and new players, and lofty organizational priorities regarding culture and environment, would somehow come out of the gate and be successful competitively against a murderer’s row of initial opponents. In seven of their first 11 games, the Canucks have faced a team that has either won the Stanley Cup or been to the final in the last five years. And like 7-Eleven, the Canucks’ team defence has been open at all hours, surrendering an NHL-worst 51 goals. As Johnson predicted, they have been punched in the face.

Former captain Brady Tkachuk was heavily booed in his return to Ottawa as a member of the Florida Panthers , four months after requesting a trade from the only NHL team he'd ever known. Spectators also drowned out a video tribute to the former captain with profane chants. Tkachuk seemed to revel in the atmosphere. He raised his stick in acknowledgement during the tribute and waved at fans with his trademark grin. Drafted fourth overall in 2018, Tkachuk spent eight seasons with the Senators. A fan favourite for much of his tenure, he helped Ottawa return to the playoffs in 2025, ending a seven-year drought. Tkachuk and his brother Matthew faced criticism over their "Wingmen" podcast, while Brady's decision to attend a White House celebration following the U.S. men's Olympic gold medal also drew backlash. Speculation about Tkachuk's future in Ottawa intensified late last season. Less than two months later, Tkachuk was traded to the Panthers. items.summary: Tkachuk explained ahead of his return to Ottawa Wednesday that there were both personal and professional reasons he would not have re-signed with the Senators.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect When the NHL schedule was released over the summer, Oct. 21 stood out immediately due to the matchup in Canada’s capital between the Ottawa Senators and Florida Panthers , set to mark Brady Tkachuk’s return to Ottawa after he requested and received a trade in June. On Wednesday night, after a few months of waiting, the Ottawa faithful had their chance to let their former captain know how they felt about his decision. To the surprise of absolutely nobody, Tkachuk was showered with boos – and, of course, “Brady Sucks” chants prior to the game. Senators general manager Steve Staios revealed shortly after the trade, which took place during the 2026 NHL Draft, that Tkachuk had specifically requested to be moved elsewhere. Before the game on Wednesday, Tkachuk addressed reporters , citing both personal and professional reasons that he had no plans to re-sign with the Senators upon the conclusion of his contract. Still, Tkachuk attempted to strike a conciliatory tone with the fans who once adored him. On his podcast with his older brother Matthew, Brady announced that any jerseys tossed on to the ice during the game would be donated to the Ottawa Boys and Girls Club . “I just know how special it’s going to be for me just to be there in front of the fans that supported me and were there for eight years ever since I got in the league, always supporting me and my family,” he said. The younger Tkachuk brother got off to a slow start with his new team before making his presence felt in historic fashion last week. items.summary: The Predators are potential playoff contenders, but need a little more strength on their back end.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Alan Poizner-Imagn Images Teams across the NHL are gauging their worth in the early weeks of the 2026-27 season, with one team potentially looking to bolster its back end. The Nashville Predators entered the 2026-27 season after fighting for a Wild Card spot in the Western Conference last season, ultimately coming up short. Yet, with new general manager Chris MacFarland coming into the fold, there are expectations that the team in Smashville would be back in Stanley Cup Playoff contention once again. However, through eight games, the Preds have struggled, winning just three times thus far. Even with experience on the back end, headlined by captain Roman Josi, Nashville needs to be a little stronger in their own zone if it wants to hang with the best in the conference. On Wednesday’s edition of Daily Faceoff LIVE , David Pagnotta joined Tyler Yaremchuk and Carter Hutton to discuss how the Predators are going to revamp their defense corps. David Pagnotta: The blue line is definitely something that they want to kind of augment a little bit. There is a veteran defenseman that they’ve had talks with about other teams, or with other teams about, excuse me, and that they’re listening on….not Roman Josi. Calm down. The Boston Bruins got a significant piece of business done by locking up one of their promising young forwards. The Bruins have agreed to a three-year, $11.85-million extension with forward Marat Khusnutdinov ($3.95 million AAV) that will keep him under contract with the team until the conclusion of the 2029-30 season. Khusnutdinov was set to become a restricted free agent at the end of the season. He has recorded two goals and five points in 10 games with the Bruins this season. The 24-year-old was originally acquired by the Bruins on March 6, 2025 from the Minnesota Wild , along with Jakub Lauko and a 2026 sixth-round pick, in exchange for Justin Brazeau. Khusnutdinov was originally selected by the Wild in second round of the 2020 NHL Draft and spent nearly three full seasons afterwards in the KHL between SKA St. Petersburg and Sochi HC. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Matt Blewett-Imagn Images The trade request saga between three-time Vezina Trophy-winning goalie Connor Hellebuyck and the Winnipeg Jets could either be resolved or reach a new pinnacle of drama soon. He’s a unique person that’s tricky to manage, whether it’s media, whether it’s interviews around the team. What is this dynamic like from the Winnipeg dressing room as the suspension lifts? And the potential plan of, like, just paying him to be a practice guy, or does he actually step foot again in that locker room and disrupt what they have going on? items.body: "I'm done, yeah," Vlasic responded when asked if he was done playing hockey by reporters on Tuesday. "Semi-retired. Not official," the former Team Canada defenceman added. Vlasic, 39, has not suited up for NHL action since playing 27 games during the 2024-25 season. He registered three points and a minus-10 rating with the Sharks that campaign, well below his usual output over his 19-year career with the franchise. As for what's next, Vlasic said he's not interested in trying to catch on with an NHL team and is instead spending his time focusing on being a "full-time dad." "I'm loving it a lot more," said Vlasic. " I've been with her everyday ... it's cool to see the evolution of it. (She's) starting to crawl, starting to motor quite a bit now, so I got my hands full." items.summary: Former Senators captain Brady Tkachuk is facing his old squad for the first time as a member of the Panthers on Wednesday night. Ryan Dixon has the story from Kanata ahead of the emotionally charged affair.
items.body: KANATA, Ont. — Ottawa Senators fans can do their worst; it’s not going to change the way Brady Tkachuk feels about them or the city and team he used to represent. Tkachuk, the former Senators captain, is facing his old squad for the first time as a member of the Florida Panthers on Wednesday night. There’s an overwhelming sense fans at Kanata’s Canadian Tire Centre will not be kind to the guy who informed the club last summer — with two years remaining on his contract — that he would not be re-signing in Ottawa. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect For most of the past two decades, the Boston Bruins being one of the Eastern Conference’s top teams was not news. Led by Hall-of-Fame captains Zdeno Chara and Patrice Bergeron and a seemingly endless procession of Vezina-caliber goaltenders, the Bruins missed the playoffs only twice between 2008 and 2024, reaching the Stanley Cup Final three times and piling up six division titles. The Black and Gold were so dominant that ‘only’ lifting the grail once this century is more often viewed with wistful disappointment than pride in that 2011 triumph. The early 2025 identity crisis that saw stalwarts Brad Marchand, Brandon Carlo, and Charlie Coyle traded out of Beantown threatened to end Boston’s lengthy reign of terror in the Eastern Conference for good, but the Bruins didn’t even have the decency to humor rival fans in Toronto , Montreal , and Carolina by staying down for the count; Boston piled up 100 points the next year to end its playoff drought at a whopping one season. To the casual fan, the B’s were good in 2025-26, they’re good now, and a strong Boston club is an inevitability on par with death and taxes. More plugged-in viewers would be less charitable in their assessment of last season’s Bruins, who looked fluky through a pair of readers, let alone under a microscope. Zito, who grew up about 15 minutes north of Milwaukee in Whitefish Bay, Wisconsin, plans to take advantage of the mini break before the Panthers play the Blackhawks on Sunday to get to American Family Field to watch the Brewers’ first World Series appearance in 44 years. “Yeah, I'm trying to get tickets,” Zito said Tuesday. “So, we'll absolutely get going.” Zito had an inside view the last time the Brewers were in the World Series in 1982. Now 62, Zito at the time was a batboy and clubhouse attendant for the Brewers from 1981-83. Zito raced home with his son, Billy, following the Panthers’ 3-2 overtime win against the Vancouver Canucks last Thursday in time to see the final outs of the Brewers’ pennant-clinching 6-4 victory against the Los Angeles Dodgers in Game 4 of the National League Championship Series. items.body: Connor McDavid 's torrid start to the 2026-27 season hit a new level on Tuesday night. As the Edmonton Oilers held off the Minnesota Wild for a 4-3 overtime win on home ice, McDavid dished out a trio of assists, including his 20th helper of the year on Evan Bouchard's game-winning goal. It set the NHL record for most assists through the first nine games of a season, per Sportsnet Stats. Already a three-time Hart Trophy winner, McDavid appears to have his eyes set on a fourth early into his 12th campaign. McDavid now has an NHL-leading 26 points and has helped the Oilers break out to a 7-1-1 record as they look to bounce back from a disappointing first-round exit in the Stanley Cup Playoffs last spring. That blistering start puts the 29-year-old on pace for 242 points over 84 games, which would shatter the NHL record of 215 set by Wayne Gretzky in the 1985-86 season. McDavid's previous career high came in 2022-23, when he scored 64 goals and dished out 89 assists for 153 points. Numbers that seem to have a small chance of standing up beyond this season, so long as the superstar centre can keep producing at this historic pace.

items.body: DALLAS — Mikko Rantanen scored in overtime to complete a hat trick, and the Dallas Stars beat Boston 3-2 on Tuesday night to snap the Bruins' five-game winning streak. It was the 11th career three-goal game for Rantanen and his first in the regular season since joining the Stars in a trade during the 2024-25 season. He became the fourth Stars player with an overtime hat trick since the team moved to Dallas for the 1993-94 season. Rantanen got his first goal early in the second period to tie the game at 1-1, and he tied it again in the third. His winner came on the power play at 3:52 of overtime when he did some nifty stick work in close and fired a shot past the left shoulder of Jeremy Swayman, who earlier in the extra period stopped Wyatt Johnston on two breakaway attempts 10 seconds apart and finished with 22 saves. Jake Oettinger stopped 18 shots for Dallas (5-3-1) in its third straight win. Matthew Poitras and James Hagens scored for the Bruins (7-2-1), who concluded their Western Conference trip at 3-0-1. Boston went 0 for 4 on the power play against Dallas, which came in allowing an NHL-best 1.5 goals per game and had the fourth-best penalty kill in the league. The Stars have allowed one power-play goal on opponents' last 25 chances. Roope Hintz had a shot from in close deflect off the leg of Boston’s Charlie McAvoy, and the loose puck ricocheted directly to Rantanen, who poked it past Swayman with 6:22 left in regulation to tie it at 2-all.

Jet Greaves stopped 14 shots before being pulled in the second period after allowing his fifth goal. Cam Talbot stopped two of the three shots he faced in relief. Christiansen’s first goal of the season at 2:38 of the first period gave Columbus the early lead. Marchenko, who faced unrelenting boos in his first visit since being traded by Columbus, pulled Toronto even with a power-play goal at 8:16. Kent Johnson appeared to put Columbus ahead with a one-timer, but the goal was waved off because time had expired. The second period was all Toronto, starting with goals 46 seconds apart from Nylander and Matthews, who has 16 goals and 27 points in 21 career games against the Blue Jackets. Colton Sissons’ assist on Nylander's goal extended his points streak to four games. Cowan’s short-handed goal gave the Maple Leafs a three-goal lead at 6:48 before Roslovic made it 5-1 and chased Greaves from the net at 12:03. According to Helene St. James of The Detroit Free Press , the Detroit Red Wings center has expanded his list of potential trade destinations to 10 teams. Larkin made headlines back in June, as the Washington Township, Mich. native asked to be traded from his hometown team . Originally, the list of teams he’d be willing to go to was just the Florida Panthers , Minnesota Wild , and Vegas Golden Knights . Even after Yzerman stepped down as GM, Larkin still wanted out of Detroit. In September, it was reported that Larkin expressed interest in being sent to the Colorado Avalanche , Tampa Bay Lightning , or Washington Capitals . Yet, in the past few weeks, nothing has changed, with Larkin having to play games for the Wings to keep his trade value intact. Now, according to St. James, Larkin would be willing to be traded to the Carolina Hurricanes , New Jersey Devils or even the upstart Utah Mammoth . He has the ability to determine his future home, as Larkin has a full no-trade clause on his current contract, which carries an AAV of $8.7 million through the 2030-31 campaign. items.body: Dylan Larkin has reportedly opened up his trade request to include more teams. Helene St. James of The Detroit Free Press reports that Larkin's trade list now includes the Florida Panthers, Minnesota Wild, Vegas Golden Knights, Dallas Stars, Washington Capitals, Carolina Hurricanes, Utah Mammoth, Tampa Bay Lightning, New Jersey Devils and Colorado Avalanche. The now-former captain of the Red Wings requested a trade in the spring and St. James reported at the time that he was only open to a move to the Panthers, Wild and Golden Knights. While former general manager Steve Yzerman fielded calls for Larkin, once he was removed from his post on July 15, those talks stalled while the Red Wings searched for a new head of hockey operations. That search is ongoing but Shawn Horcoff was elevated to interim general manager in September and seemingly has the authority to complete a Larkin trade. St. James reports one of the reasons a trade has not happened yet is that the Red Wings continue to ask for "value-now" players instead of a package of prospects and draft picks. One team notably not on Larkin's trade list is the Montreal Canadiens, even after Canadiens fans chanted "we want Larkin!" during a recent visit by the Red Wings. Larkin has one goal and three points in six games for the Red Wings this season after missing training camp with an upper-body injury.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It has been a disappointing start to the year for the NHL’s three Californian teams. The Los Angeles Kings are the last winless team in the league, and both the Anaheim Ducks and San Jose Sharks sit at NHL .500 and comfortably back of the pace in the Pacific Division. While the Kings have an aging roster and are entrenched in a downward trend, both the Ducks and Sharks have young, talented cores and entered the year with high expectations. While the Ducks were handicapped by the offer sheet to Leo Carlsson, they were still a playoff team a year ago, and the standard was to repeat that performance at least. Meanwhile in the Bay Area, the hype around this young core led by Macklin Celebrini has reached a fever pitch, and general manager Mike Grier added plenty of veterans to a group that pushed for a playoff spot last year. On Tuesday’s episode of Daily Faceoff LIVE , host former NHL goaltender Carter Hutton was joined by former NHL video coach Steve Peters to discuss the disappointing starts to the year for the two young, promising teams out of California. Carter Hutton : Right now we’re watching two young teams that we thought were going to come out flying, the Sharks and the Ducks, and these are teams that I’ve been kind of watching… the Sharks don’t have a regulation win, Petey, and the Ducks have dropped their last three being outscored 13-6. What are your concerns about these younger teams who were supposed to take the step forward in the Pacific Division? items.body: Register Login Kings Activate Mats Zuccarello By Brennan McClain | at October 20, 2026 1:00 pm The winless Los Angeles Kings are getting a key reinforcement back to their forward corps. According to a team announcement , the Kings have activated winger Mats Zuccarello from the injured reserve. Los Angeles had two openings on their 23-man roster, so no corresponding transaction was necessary. Simply put, the Kings need all the help they can get. After the Philadelphia Flyers defeated the Ottawa Senators this past Saturday, the Los Angeles Kings remained the only team yet to win their first game of the 2026-27 season. The Kings are dead last in the NHL three weeks into the season. There are two main reasons for that. First, Los Angeles has gotten dismal play from between the pipes, with the tandem of Darcy Kuemper and Anton Forsberg managing an .861 SV%. Hardly conducive to winning. Secondly, the Kings struggle to score, which has been a problem for a while. Last season, despite making the postseason for the fifth consecutive year, Los Angeles finished 29th in scoring. This season, albeit early, the Kings are 31st in scoring, just ahead of the Flyers. Fortunately, with Zuccarello returning, this should improve. He’s been limited to one assist in two games this season due to an undisclosed injury. However, even on the wrong side of 30, Zuccarello is one year removed from scoring 15 goals and 54 points in 59 games with the Minnesota Wild. It will take more than Zuccarello to turn things around, but there is a silver lining for the Kings. They have played the fewest games in the league so far, so there is still time to recover.

The Washington Capitals have activated defenseman Matt Roy off injured reserve, with head coach Spencer Carbery announcing that he’ll be in the lineup on Tuesday night, when the Capitals play host to the Los Angeles Kings . Roy has missed the past six games due to a lower-body injury that he suffered back on Oct. 3 against the Tampa Bay Lightning . The Capitals have been solid during that time, going 4-2-0, winning each of their past two games, including a 4-2 victory over the New Jersey Devils this past Saturday. Roy was placed on injured reserve a little over a week later to make room for fellow blueliner Justin Holl. Roy’s injury came in the second game of the 2026-27 campaign. He was in the lineup for the season opener on Friday night, when Washington came away with a 5-2 win over the defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes . Roy played 22:29 in the victory, but didn’t put his name on the scoresheet. The 31-year-old is in his third season in the U.S. capital. After five seasons with the Kings, the Detroit native signed with the Capitals as a free agent, inking a six-year, $34.5 million contract with the team in July 2024. After five consecutive seasons with at least 20 points , Roy’s production took a dip last season on a Washington team that struggled, posting just two goals and 19 points in 79 games. In 518 regular-season games in the NHL, Roy has notched 29 goals and 120 assists for 149 points, with another eight points in 28 Stanley Cup Playoff contests. Puck drop between the Capitals (5-3-0) and Kings is scheduled for 7 p.m. ET.

items.body: Johnson says coaches must find ways for 2026 Draft picks McKenna, Stenberg, Smits to earn minutes The Coaches Room is a regular feature throughout the 2026-27 season by former NHL coaches and assistants who turn their critical gaze to the game and explain it through the lens of a teacher. In this edition, Craig Johnson, a former assistant with the Anaheim Ducks and Ontario of the American Hockey League, and development coach with the Los Angeles Kings, writes about giving ice time to young players, specifically three teenagers selected in the 2026 NHL Draft, the challenges associated with it and why it all relates to the development path of the player. Accountability is a big thing in the NHL and it must be maintained. But teenagers like Gavin McKenna with the Toronto Maple Leafs, Alberts Smits with the New York Rangers and Ivar Stenberg with the San Jose Sharks are your future, and that's where handing out minutes becomes a balancing act for a coach. You're feeling the pressure to win now, especially in big markets like Toronto and New York. But you're working with players who are vitally important to the future of the team, both later this season and long beyond it, and who are probably making mistakes in the details of the game. You see it all the time. You think these players are finely tuned when they get to the NHL because of how they performed to become top prospects in their draft year. With the exception of Foerster, who played Saturday night versus the Ottawa Senators , all of their respective absences have been for multiple games. Speaking with Flyers sources Monday morning, Daily Faceoff was told that the team’s newfound success could lead to some roster changes moving forward. items.title: Canadiens’ Adam Engstrom, Jakub Dobes draw in against Sharks
items.body: The Montreal Canadiens are shaking up their lineup despite coming off a win. Defenceman Adam Engstrom will draw in for David Reinbacher while Jakub Dobes returns to the net in favour of Jacob Fowler on Tuesday against the San Jose Sharks, head coach Martin St. Louis told reporters . On the blue line, St. Louis said the move did not have to do with Reinbacher's play, instead choosing to rotate both players to ensure playing time. Engstrom, 22, is averaging 11 minutes of ice time across four games this season while being held off the scoresheet. Reinbacher, 21, played 9:09 in his season debut Saturday in a 4-3 win over the Buffalo Sabres. Fowler made 23 saves in that victory, building on a strong start to the season in which he holds a .900 save percentage and 2.16 goals-against average. Dobes, meanwhile, has struggled after his breakout last season, posting an .842 save percentage and 4.63 GAA in four appearances. The Sharks are coming off a 3-1 loss to the Toronto Maple Leafs on Monday.

items.title: Panthers’ Jacob Markstrom to miss 10-14 days; Cooper Black recalled
items.summary: Markstrom was injured during practice on Tuesday, leading Florida to call up Cooper Black from AHL Charlotte.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Isabella Frias-Imagn Images Some unwanted news in the Sunshine State. When speaking to the media on Tuesday, Florida Panthers head coach Paul Maurice announced that goaltender Jacob Markstrom is expected to miss the next 10-14 days after getting injured in practice on Monday. The Panthers called up fellow netminder Cooper Black from their American Hockey League affiliate, the Charlotte Checkers. Maurice added that Black will make his NHL debut on the team’s four-game road trip, which begins Wednesday night against the rival Ottawa Senators . Maurice didn’t go into detail about what has knocked Markstrom out of action, only stating that he was hit with a puck, which kept him off the ice on Tuesday as well. It had to have hit the Swedish backstop in a soft spot to be worth keeping him on the shelf for possibly two weeks. Markstrom has been solid in his return to Florida thus far. In six starts, the 36-year-old has a record of 3-1-1, with a 2.21 goals-against average, a .897 save percentage and one shutout. The Panthers reacquired him and Angus Crookshank this past offseason from the New Jersey Devils , trading Evan Rodrigues, Jesper Boqvist and Ben Steeves to make it happen. Whenever Black makes his first NHL start, he’ll become the tallest netminder in league history. The Alpena, Mich. native stands at 6-foot-8 and is coming off an impressive rookie season with the Checkers, where he went 25-13-4, helping his team finish third in the AHL’s Atlantic Division. items.title: Brady Tkachuk, Senators ready to get first reunion over with
items.summary: Wednesday will be Tkachuk’s first game back in Ottawa since getting traded to the Panthers.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The Florida Panthers are hardly fan favorites when they visit opposing arenas, but the crowd for Wednesday’s road game against the Ottawa Senators should be especially antagonistic. Wednesday will be former Senators captain Brady Tkachuk’s first game back in Ottawa since requesting and getting granted a trade to the Panthers this past offseason. Fan bases usually don’t take it in stride when a star player decides to orchestrate his exit from their team. Just ask John Tavares about visiting the New York Islanders , or Jack Eichel about going back to play the Buffalo Sabres . Wednesday night should be no different, and Senators fans will have plenty of vitriol in store for Tkachuk. On Tuesday’s episode of Daily Faceoff LIVE , hosts Carter Hutton and Steve Peters were joined by Brent Wallace to discuss the expectations heading into Tkachuk’s return to Ottawa. Carter Hutton: With Brady’s return, what is the vibe in Ottawa? What is it like around the rink and the fanbase with everything that’s been going on with him? And obviously seeing his natural hat trick success going on in Florida. Brent Wallace: Yeah, his first star of the week couldn’t have come at a worse time for the Ottawa Senators fans, if you will. They were hoping he was going to continue that pace of no points in five games. This isn’t about the players, necessarily. The players are kind of saying like, “Yeah, we’re interested a little bit” or “We’re not paying attention.” This is basically the fans of Ottawa having one last chance to voice their displeasure, or pleasure if they have any, with the way Brady was here for the last eight years.
